text.p: These are the leading stories in the Namibian press on Thursday.
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Four more Chinese construction companies will probably be awarded Government tenders next year, according to industry sources. There have been complaints of unfair competition from local firms. Eight Chinese construction companies are known to be operating in Namibia.
- The current chair of the Law Reform Commission, Bience Gawanas has been officially appointed Ombudsman.
- Tom Alweendo will be the first Namibian governor of the Bank of Namibia from January 1. He is currently deputy governor.
- The chairperson of the Law Reform Commission, Bience Gawanas has been appointed as new Ombudsman.
- The Chinese government has granted Namibia an interest free loan of N$15 million which is to be used primarily for irrigation projects.
